one_month_reasoning: Inside the window to 2026-11-04: (1) MOD Q2 FY27 results. The date is not yet announced (no EDGAR filing as of Oct 6); last year's Q2 call was Oct 29, so about Oct 27-29 is very likely. This is the first continuing-operations FY27 guide and the test of whether Data Centers margin recovers from Q1's 14.8%. To meet the slide guide of DC earnings growth above 85% (at least ~$397M), DC must earn ~$115M a quarter for the rest of the year, against $51.7M in Q1. A standalone guide below that is a real risk, but so is a relief rally if supply has cleared. (2) Peer prints: Vertiv (~Oct 22), Trane, Carrier and JCI (late Oct/early Nov). Their DC orders have been very strong, which supports sentiment. (3) Hyperscaler Q3 calls (~Oct 28-30) with first 2027 capex indications. (4) The 8-K/A pro forma is due ~Oct 7; it should be a non-event. The Nov 18 Investor Day with new multi-year targets falls after the window. Two-sided event risk with no edge, so I stay neutral: lognormal median ~$183.5, monthly sigma ~19% (71%/3.5 = 20%, trimmed slightly because spin noise has gone).

The multiples are ~12% and ~4% below the 8-core-peer medians (19.34x / 25.93x, re-derived from filings by the citation audit 2026-10-06) and inside the 10-peer range.

bear.story: The Q2 standalone guide lands well below the >85% DC earnings growth, DC margins stay in the mid-teens, and the large hyperscaler (~11% of FY26 consolidated sales per the 10-K; ~30% of DC if all DC, an estimate) defers chiller pull-ins. 45C warm-water designs cut chiller content per MW in new halls while Trane, JCI and Carrier capacity pressures pricing. A 2027 capex digestion compresses the multiple to ~13x on ~$480M NTM EBITDA, less net debt, = ~$115.

base.story: Supply issues fade, DC margins reach ~20% from Q2-Q3, and FY27 RemainCo EBITDA is ~$460M (just under the guide). The $4B LTA and broad DC demand drive DC sales +35% in FY28. Oct-2027 NTM EBITDA is ~$655M at 17x and EPS ~$7.80 at 25x.

bull.story: Hyperscaler 2027 capex follows the high path and the Nov-18 Investor Day sets credible targets (DC 50%+ growth, low-20s margins) that MOD then delivers. MOD adds a second LTA, chillers stay needed for trim and hybrid cooling, and NTM EBITDA reaches ~$790M at ~19.5x, the core peer median.

comps_summary.peer_range: 10 peers: fwd P/E 14.18x (LII) to 29.79x (FIX); fwd EV/EBITDA 11.25x (LII) to 28.23x (VRT). Core-8 (excluding ETN and FIX, whose DC exposure is electrical or contracting rather than thermal equipment): P/E median 25.93x, EV/EBITDA median 19.33x. Basis: P/E = Oct-5 close / NTM consensus EPS (stockanalysis this-year/next-year estimates, calendarised; JCI FY Sep-2027). EV/EBITDA uses one formula for every peer: TTM EV/EBITDA computed from the peer's 10-Q/10-K (GAAP operating earnings + D&A; debt, cash, shares) and the Oct-5 close, / (1 + average of 3Y consensus revenue and EPS CAGR, stockanalysis). This is a growth-adjusted proxy, not vendor forward EBITDA. Daikin and Munters were dropped because their consensus is on a different basis.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 17x NTM EV/EBITDA and 25x P/E: ~12% / ~4% below the core-8 medians, ~20% / ~6% below the 10-peer medians, and well inside both ranges. MOD today trades ~18x NTM (Oct-26 to Sep-27) RemainCo EBITDA of ~$555M (estimate from my FY27E/FY28E builds; EV ~$10.0B = 53.2M x $182.91 + ~$280M).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount rests on structural features that will not change within 12 months. (a) Concentration: per the FY26 10-K, one global technology customer was ~11% of consolidated sales (estimates: ~$350M = 0.11 x $3,181.1M; ~30% of DC sales if all of it is DC; ~17% of FY26 DC+CHVAC sales of $2,082.0M), and the top ten were 49%. The $4B chiller LTA deepens this exposure; diversified peers (TT, JCI, CARR, ETN) have no comparable single-customer weight. I dropped my round-1 'half of DC capacity' figure, which was not in the filings. (b) Margins: DC adj. EBITDA margin was 14.8% in Q1 and ~19% in FY26, against VRT/TT GAAP operating margins of ~19%/~18% (TTM to 2026-06-30: VRT $2,174.6M / $11,479.6M, TT $3,984.7M / $22,209.9M, 10-Q XBRL); scale is a fraction of TT/JCI/CARR, each of which is multiplying DC chiller capacity. (c) Execution: the Q1 supply-driven miss is a demonstrated weakness, not a forecast. (d) Product mix: MOD's DC business is chiller-heavy and therefore the most exposed to 45C warm-water designs (it fell -17% on the Vera Rubin remark vs -8% for TT/JCI). There is no premium for top-quartile growth because VRT, NVT, AAON and FIX are priced for similar growth.

thesis_break_reason: At $125 the equity is ~$6.65B and EV ~$6.9B, ~15x FY27E and ~11.5x FY28E RemainCo EBITDA, at the bottom of the peer range (LII 11.6x) for a business guiding DC growth of 60-80%. Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental broke: the $4B LTA was deferred or lost, chiller attach rates fell structurally as 45C designs scaled, share was lost to the expanding big-HVAC capacity, or AI capex retrenched. Ordinary volatility (71% realised) alone is unlikely to explain it. The level is near the spin-adjusted Jan-2026 Vera Rubin panic lows.

reasoning: RemainCo (Data Centers + Commercial HVAC) only; the THRM stake (~$14/sh) is already out of the price. Round-2 changes, all checked against primary filings: Q1 corporate was -$23.0M (Ex.99.1), so I now use -$80M/yr. Net debt is $432.9M - $156.0M = ~$277M at close (Ex.99.1, 8-K); the 8-K/A is still unfiled per the EDGAR index. Concentration comes from the 10-K: one customer ~11% of consolidated sales, top ten 49%; my 'half of DC capacity' claim is withdrawn. The Q1 slides guide Commercial HVAC sales at +5-10%, not the +12% I used, and DC earnings growth at >85%. The Nov-18 Investor Day is confirmed. FY27E RemainCo EBITDA is ~$461M, below the guide-implied ~$490M after Q1's 14.8% DC margin. Oct-2027 NTM is ~$655M (FY28E $600M, FY29E $725M). The industry lane still says demand is strong (TT applied bookings +130%, CARR DC orders ~4x, JCI Americas +37%, Munters orders +137% with book-to-bill 2.3x and large multi-year DC chiller orders, 66 GW NA under construction at ~1% vacancy). The same sources show competitor capacity growth and warm-water/chiller-free CDU marketing (DCX), so I keep DC growth below management's 50-70%. Comps: rebuilt on 10 US peers with one formula (TTM EV/EBITDA over average 3Y growth). Medians are 20.9x / 28.6x, or 19.2x / 27.6x on the core-8 the supervisor used; Daikin and Munters are dropped. I keep 17x / 25x, a ~10% persistent discount for concentration, lower margin, execution and chiller-substitution exposure. Fair value $198 (from $196). Distribution: 50/50 blend of a scenario mixture (bear $115 25%, base $198 50%, bull $285 25%, each lognormal) and one lognormal (median $192, sigma 0.52, consistent with ~71% realised vol damped for horizon mean-reversion). Ladder median ~$194, P(>= today) ~55%. I broadly agree with the supervisor's fair value (~$204); I sit slightly lower because I take a slightly lower NTM EBITDA ($655M vs $675M) and less deleveraging.
